subject: Geo control pack request & private peering readiness for MediSentry (SIG/CAIQ)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Tran <alyssa.tran@medsentry.io>, security@medsentry.io
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Geo control pack request & private peering readiness for MediSentry (SIG/CAIQ)

Hi Alyssa / MediSentry security team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — excited about the pilot. Legal is requesting a small evidence pack so your procurement group can complete their SIG/CAIQ review. Can you confirm whether the items below are sufficient, or list anything else you need? Our ask is to capture minimal artifacts that prove our hosting boundary and private peering options for the pilot.

Requested items (can be attachments or links):
- Short-form attestation letter: statement that Redwood will confine customer workload for the pilot to US regions (us-east-1 / us-west-2) and private VPC peering if deployed as "Private".
- SIG/CAIQ extract: sections related to network isolation, encryption, region controls (PDF okay).
- Evidence of private peering readiness: sample peering checklist + expected timeline for test peering.
- SOC 2 summary or link (if available) and contact for SOC2 report access.

Timeline: MediSentry procurement is hoping to close the pilot paperwork this week. If you can share the deliverables above by EOD Thu (Aug 20), we can route the MSA + security addendum for signature.

Attachments we will provide from our side once you confirm: Redwood_PRIVATE_Deploy_Runbook (network/ops runbook) and a short attestation template for you to countersign.

Thanks — will loop in Irene for the technical runbook.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

[attachment stubs: Redwood_Private_Deploy_Runbook.pdf, Redwood_Attestation_shortform.docx]

From: Alyssa Tran <alyssa.tran@medsentry.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medsentry.io
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Geo control pack request & private peering readiness for MediSentry (SIG/CAIQ)

Marissa — thanks, this is helpful. Short answers up front: yes, the list covers what procurement needs for the pilot. We can accept a short attestation (one page) and a runbook + peering checklist. A couple of clarifying Qs below:

1) For the attestation: do you have a standard template, or do you prefer us to draft a countersign-friendly paragraph?
2) For peering testing: do you support a cross-connect window, or is the recommended flow a VPN-to-VPN handoff for the pilot? Our infra team prefers an IPsec tunnel initially to avoid early cross-connect work.
3) Is the SOC2 report available via an on-demand link or NDA? We will likely need the SOC2 bridge letter.

Attached: MediSentry_SIG_v1.pdf (our security team attached their SIG baseline — this is their internal reference; won’t share broadly).

We can target EOD Thu, but if Redwood can provide the runbook + attestation template by lunchtime tomorrow, that helps.

Thanks,
Alyssa Tran
Head of Procurement | MediSentry
alyssa.tran@medsentry.io
(212) 555-0158

[attachment stubs: MediSentry_SIG_v1.pdf]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Tran <alyssa.tran@medsentry.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Geo control pack request & private peering readiness for MediSentry (SIG/CAIQ)

Hi Alyssa / Marissa,

Looping Karthik for the networking details. Quick summary of what Redwood will attach/send by 14:00 PDT today:
- Redwood_Private_Deploy_Runbook.pdf — includes network topology, KV cache handling, and peering validation steps (we mark the sections relevant to private mode).
- vpc-peering-checklist.xlsx — our ops checklist used for pilot peering tests (expected 2–4 hour validation window for IPsec test).
- Redwood_Attestation_shortform.docx — one-page attestation that we can countersign.
- Link to SOC2 summary and process to request the full report under NDA: https://storage.redwood.com/soc2/Redwood_SOC2_Report_Q1_2026.pdf

Answers to your Qs:
1) Attestation: we will send our standard one-page template. You are welcome to redline; our legal prefers countersigning that doc to speed process.
2) Peering testing: for pilot we recommend IPsec VPN to start (no cross-connect needed). Once pilot is validated, we can move to private peering via AWS Direct Connect or equivalent. The runbook includes both flows and a checklist for each.
3) SOC2 access: summary link above; full report available after an NDA — I can introduce you to our compliance contact if you need the bridge letter.

Next steps we propose:
- You review the attestation template and return an initial countersign by Fri morning if possible.
- Schedule a 60-minute network validation call next Mon (Aug 23) with our infra engineers — suggested time: 10:00 PDT.

Karthik — can you confirm we have region-level KMS separation documented (US-only partition for pilot) so Alyssa can pass to their compliance reviewers? I’ll attach the small runbook excerpt showing the KMS flow.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
+1 (650) 555-0134
